standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the end of the counted proof (lines 35785-35787)

core_obligations: Recall that the naive cotangent complex is built from the kernel I of the canonical presentation of S over R[S] (proof lines 35782-35784).
Observe that the polynomial algebra over the colimit is the colimit of the polynomial algebras, and likewise the kernel is the colimit of the individual kernels (proof lines 35785-35787).
Conclude that the two-term complex over the colimit is the colimit of the complexes over the index set (proof lines 35787-35788).
proof_roadmap: Write the complex from a presentation so that its terms are kernels and polynomial algebras (proof lines 35781-35784).
Commute the colimit with both constructions and conclude (proof lines 35785-35789).
difficulty_reason: For a directed system of ring maps the lemma states that the naive cotangent complex of the colimit is the colimit of the naive cotangent complexes (statement lines 35773-35779). The proof does not verify the universal property of the complex or construct comparison maps by hand: it recalls that the complex is built from the kernel I of the canonical presentation, notes that the polynomial algebra and that kernel both commute with the directed colimit, and reads the conclusion off termwise (proof lines 35781-35789). Recognising that the definition reduces the question to two colimit commutations is the content of the argument. H2.
